items.headline: Chardonnay Shade leaves a mystery date's car without her clutch; eight secrets now loose in Astoria
items.body: Saturday, 1 AM: Chardonnay slips out the back of Velvet Static with someone in a hoodie. By sunrise her clutch is empty and everything in it is scattered across the neighborhood, each piece pointing at a different celebrity. Sal at the deli saw the driver first. Join from Tasks, then Hunt. It ends Sunday at midnight. Somebody in this city knows who was in that back seat.

items.headline: Chardonnay Shade: "There was no car." The driver: "There was a car."
items.body: In a 3 AM confessional, Chardonnay insists she "walked home alone, in heels, to Astoria." Velvet Static is in Long Island City. Asked whether Chardonnay left alone, Mags the bartender poured herself a very long glass of water and said, "Next question." Then she laughed. Then she said it again.

items.headline: Dunk Daniels shows up to practice in one sneaker and one hotel slipper
items.body: The man owns 400 pairs. He arrived (late) wearing one high-top and one terry-cloth slipper. Asked where the other shoe was, he said "ask Saturday" and put his headphones on. Sneaker forums have opened a thread called "SIZE 15???" and it already has nine hundred pages.

items.headline: Leaked: Lunaria's DMs to a contact saved as "B. 🚗" say "u left something in the car"
items.body: The screenshots surfaced Tuesday. The full message reads: "u left something in the car. not giving it back." Her team says it's "from a music video." There is no music video. Brock Squarejaw, asked if he owns a car, said he "does his own driving" and walked into a lamppost. Nobody has asked what was left behind. Yet.

items.headline: Ask Lola: "I saw my friend get into a car with someone famous. Do I tell?"
items.body: "Hon, you saw a car, not a contract. Text your friend one word, 'well?', and then wait like a lady. If she tells you, it's a secret. If you tell anyone else, it's a headline, and you're the villain in her next confessional. Choose your episode carefully." Lola Lowdown

items.headline: Skyler Beta's privacy app "Vault" accidentally posts everyone's unsent drafts
items.body: It was supposed to hide your unsent messages. For 40 minutes on Wednesday, it published them. Highlights: Chad Kensington's "hey big investor" (sent to his mom) and one draft from a user called not_chardonnay that just says "was it the hoodie?" Skyler calls it "radical transparency." Skyler also owns a gray hoodie. Just saying.

items.headline: Peyton Pastel's car-deal tryout photo has someone hiding in the back seat
items.body: Lavender coupe, golden hour, Gantry Plaza: the dream shot for the car company she's been begging for. Then fans zoomed in. Someone in a hood is ducking behind the headrest. Peyton deleted it in four minutes and posted an apology in six. Inez, who took it, says only: "I photograph what's in front of me. And behind."

items.headline: DJ Polaroid draws his first real crowd; all forty of them face the door
items.body: Someone posted that the mystery hoodie from Saturday would be at Hellgate Hall. Forty people showed up for the 7 PM slot and watched the entrance for two hours. Rocco the bouncer says the hoodie never came, "or came in a different hoodie." DJ Polaroid is calling it his breakthrough. He would like to know who to thank.

items.headline: Brock Squarejaw and Dunk Daniels spotted in the same gray hoodie, same deli, eleven minutes apart
items.body: Sal confirms both ordered a chopped cheese, both paid cash and both asked, very casually, whether anybody had dropped off "a little bag." Also Sal, the cat, hissed at only one of them. Sal won't say which. "I run a deli, not a podcast," he said, then took a call from a podcast.

items.headline: Gus says he saw the car on Saturday, then starts talking about 1987
items.body: Asked who was in the back seat, Gus nodded slowly, pointed at the bridge and told a forty-minute story about a 1987 sedan and a girl named Dolores. Witnesses say the story ended with two words: "same hoodie." He has since gone back to his bench and refuses to explain what that means.

items.headline: Chase Clout's stream went dark for 47 minutes last Saturday, his first break in three years
items.body: Chat noticed. Chat always notices. He came back in a different hoodie, holding a scratch card from a Flushing lotto shop, with no explanation. Asked where he'd been, he said "chat, chat, CHAT" and changed the subject. Benny at Lucky Star says he "doesn't remember Saturday." Benny remembers everything.

items.headline: Tiff claims she was the mystery date; her 312 followers demand proof
items.body: Her proof is a photo of a car. Any car. It's parked outside Steinway Fresh Mart and has a ticket on it. Tiff says "the vibes match." Chardonnay, through her publicist, replied "Who?", which Tiff has reposted nine times as "acknowledgment." The real date, wherever they are, has said nothing at all.

items.headline: Chardonnay Shade teases a confessional called "The Car"; the network clears a full hour
items.body: The trailer is eight seconds long: a back seat, a hand with something sparkly on one finger (or is it?) and Chardonnay whispering, "You know I can't keep a secret." Mags says she's been asked to bartend the premiere. Mags doesn't do premieres. Mags said yes. It airs next week, and so, apparently, does the name.
